correctness.rationale: Each shattered support has at most one literal per vertex. Consecutive triples force the alternating prescribed-colour pattern, and the four-consecutive support is impossible; cyclic window counting gives the exact upper bound, with the triangle treated separately. Alternating-colour selected runs in 1110 blocks provide every trace and can be joined across free vertices. An adaptive depth-(n-1) tree fixes the initial colour and queries two choices at each of the next n-2 vertices; the last is always completable. The cycle chromatic-polynomial count and colour permutation symmetry show that every root-positive branch has fewer than 2^(n-1) concepts, ruling out depth n. The standalone verifier independently checks finite cases and witnesses.

value.rationale: The same natural finite cyclic constraint family now has a complete two-invariant classification at every order and an unbounded adaptive-vs-static gap. The proof isolates the decisive cyclic four-consecutive obstruction and the symmetry-versus-online-tree mechanism. A previously studied path colouring family has different exact expressions; the closing edge forces a structural boundary change, not a cosmetic parameter substitution. The exact smallest separated cycle is n=5. This is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite case.
